links.outcome: Dialogue quality, provider burnout and image quality with vs without chatbot in randomized sub-trials
links.effect: RHP+REC improved factuality in appointment triage (4.12 vs 3.39, P<0.001), satisfaction in pre-exam preparation (3.73 vs 3.19), and burnout exhaustion (1.85 vs 2.40, P<0.01), but underperformed on empathy in radiology clinic services.
links.quote: RHP + REC group demonstrated superior dialogue quality in AT (factuality: 4.12 ± 0.86 vs. 3.39 ± 1.21, P < 0.001) and PP (satisfaction: 3.73 ± 0.11 vs. 3.19 ± 0.18, P < 0.001), with reduced burnout (exhaustion: 1.85 ± 0.91 vs. 2.40 ± 1.22, P < 0.01).

links.outcome: Chatbot empathy and emotional regulation in emotionally complex radiology clinic services
links.effect: REC scored lower than providers on empathy (3.88 ± 0.67 vs 4.42 ± 0.53, P = 0.002) and emotional regulation (3.87 ± 0.19 vs 4.12 ± 0.27, P = 0.004) in radiology clinic services.
links.quote: However, REC underperformed in empathy and emotional regulation during emotionally complex RCS (3.88 ± 0.67 vs. 4.42 ± 0.53, P = 0.002; 3.87 ± 0.19 vs. 4.12 ± 0.27, P = 0.004).

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning an LLM on domain-specific dialogue data and scenario-specific prompts (ablation showed both necessary)
Deploying an LLM chatbot to provide emotional support to cancer patients and reduce provider burnout

screen.reason: The study reports a randomized controlled trial deploying a newly developed LLM chatbot (REC) alongside radiology healthcare providers vs providers alone, measuring communication quality, provider burnout, and imaging quality. It evaluates the efficacy of the AI system itself rather than comparing a specific operational safeguard or deployment practice.
